headline: Danish startup turns childhood kite dream into rural wind power
meta_description: At 15, Andreas Okholm dreamed of harnessing wind with a kite. His Danish startup KiteX has now built a turbine generating up to 17,000 kWh annually.
summary_short: A Danish entrepreneur's teenage vision of kite-powered energy has become reality: KiteX's turbine can generate up to 17,000 kWh yearly for rural communities.
body:
A Danish entrepreneur's teenage dream of capturing wind energy with a kite has evolved into a working turbine that could power rural homes and farms. Andreas Okholm's startup, KiteX, has developed technology capable of generating up to 17,000 kilowatt-hours annually—enough to meaningfully reduce energy costs in remote areas.

What began as youthful curiosity has matured into a practical solution for communities far from traditional power grids. By combining an elegant concept with engineering persistence, KiteX demonstrates how childhood inspiration paired with determination can address real-world energy challenges. The turbine's capacity to serve rural households suggests a scalable model for distributed renewable energy.
quick_facts: Andreas Okholm founded Danish startup KiteX
Inspired by kite-wind dreams at age 15
Turbine generates up to 17,000 kWh annually
Designed for rural homes and farms
